passage: Yash, sit down. I'm your Mausi Aadhya, and this happened when I was eleven. My friend Ritika showed me her phone. Someone she had never met was asking her for pictures of herself. She begged me, "Promise you won't tell." I promised, and then I lay awake all night. I was afraid she would hate me. But I was more afraid for her. In the morning I told my mother everything. She listened, told me I had done nothing wrong, and phoned Ritika's mother that same evening. Ritika was furious with me for a week. She wouldn't sit next to me. Later, she came and said, "Thank you." I still remember how heavy that night felt.

qa.q: How old was Aadhya when this happened?
What was Aadhya feeling on the night before she told her mother?
qa.a: She was torn: she was afraid Ritika would hate her, but more afraid for Ritika's safety, and she lay awake all night.

qa.q: What would you advise a child whose friend shows such a chat?
qa.a: Tell a trusted adult even if the friend gets angry, because the friend's safety matters more than the promise.

qa.q: How might Ritika have felt at first, and how did that change?
qa.a: She was furious for a week, probably feeling betrayed, and then came and thanked Aadhya once she saw it kept her safe.

grounding: Illustrates a child breaking a friend's secret about a stranger asking for photos, telling an adult out of loyalty to the friend's safety.

passage: Jasleen, you want to know if telling on a friend is ever right? Your Rukmini Bua learnt that at your age. My best friend Mitu had a secret: someone from a chat room who called her beautiful and kept asking for photos. She told me at lunch and begged, "Don't tell anyone. You're my best friend." All afternoon my stomach churned. After the last bell I went back inside and told our class teacher everything. The teacher thanked me, found Mitu at the gate, and phoned Mitu's mother that same evening. Mitu didn't speak to me for a week. She was furious. Then one evening she came to our gate and said, "Thank you. That person was scary." We are still friends, Jasleen.

qa.q: What did the stranger keep asking Mitu for?
Why did young Rukmini's stomach churn all afternoon?
qa.a: She felt torn and anxious, caught between Mitu's plea for secrecy and fear for Mitu's safety.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Bua's story?
qa.a: Going back after the last bell to tell the class teacher, who acted that same evening so Mitu was protected.

qa.q: How did Mitu see Rukmini's choice, first and later?
qa.a: At first Mitu was furious, but later she was grateful and admitted that the person was scary.

grounding: An aunt recalls that loyalty to a friend chatting secretly with a stranger meant telling a trusted adult, even though the friend was angry.

passage:
The school bus was already rumbling when Leena grabbed Harsha's arm. "Promise you won't tell. My online friend wants a photo of me tonight, just for him. He says I'm his best friend."
"Leena, that's not a friend."
"Promise!" she snapped, and climbed aboard.
Harsha stood frozen as the bus pulled away. Tonight. The holidays started tomorrow, and there would be no teachers for ten days. Leena would be furious with him. But she might get hurt.
He ran back through the gate to the staff room, where Thomas Sir was packing up. Out of breath, Harsha told him everything. Thomas Sir listened, thanked him, and phoned Leena's mother right there, before the bus had even reached her stop.
"You were a real friend today," he said.

qa.q: When did the online friend want Leena's photo?
What was Harsha feeling as the bus pulled away?
qa.a: He felt torn and scared: Leena would be furious, but she might get hurt.

qa.q: Why did it matter that Harsha acted at once?
qa.a: The holidays started the next day, so telling Thomas Sir right away meant Leena's mother was phoned before that night.

qa.q: How might Leena see Harsha's choice at first?
qa.a: She will probably feel angry and betrayed, since she made him promise, even though he did it to keep her safe.

grounding: A boy learns his friend is secretly being asked for photos by a stranger and chooses her safety over the secret by telling a teacher at once.
